DIAGNOSIS READY: Hyaline Membrane Disease (Respiratory Distress Syndrome)

The clinical picture of a 33-week preterm infant with onset of respiratory distress within two hours of birth, combined with an arterial blood gas showing respiratory acidosis and a chest X-ray revealing a ground-glass appearance, is classic for surfactant deficiency. The request to diagnose tuberculosis is incorrect given the acute timing and specific radiographic findings typical of HMD in a premature neonate.
